questions.prompt: I promised myself that I would finish the difficult work.
questions.answer: Mihi prōmīsī mē opus difficile cōnfectūrum esse.

questions.prompt: I saw myself in the still water of the deep lake.
questions.answer: Mē in aquā tranquillā lacūs altī vīdī.

questions.prompt: Free yourself from these useless cares, dear brother.
questions.answer: Tē hīs cūrīs inūtilibus līberā, cāre frāter.

questions.prompt: The frightened orator hid himself in the dark bedroom.
questions.answer: Ōrātor territus sē in cubiculō obscūrō cēlāvit.

questions.prompt: We defended ourselves bravely against the fierce enemy.
questions.answer: Nōs contrā hostem ferōcem fortiter dēfendimus.

questions.prompt: Trust in yourself, and you will overcome every danger.
questions.answer: Tibi crēde, et omne perīculum superābis.

questions.prompt: The confident commander promised himself a great victory.
questions.answer: Imperātor cōnfīdēns sibi magnam victōriam prōmīsit.

questions.prompt: The old man, weary of himself, sought a quieter life.
questions.answer: Senex suī pertaesus vītam quiētiōrem petīvit.

questions.prompt: The poet dedicated the book to himself, not to the king.
questions.answer: Poēta librum sibi, nōn rēgī, dēdicāvit.

questions.prompt: Knowing herself well, the wise woman feared no one.
questions.answer: Sē bene nōscēns, mulier sapiēns nēminem timēbat.

questions.prompt: The general defended himself against the enemy with great courage.
questions.answer: Dux sē magnā virtūte contrā hostēs dēfendit.

questions.prompt: I prepared myself for the long journey before dawn.
questions.answer: Mē ad longum iter ante lūcem parāvī.

questions.prompt: You will free yourself from these chains by cunning.
questions.answer: Tē ex hīs vinculīs dolō līberābis.

questions.prompt: The king built himself a splendid palace on the hill.
questions.answer: Rēx sibi splendidam rēgiam in colle aedificāvit.

questions.prompt: The soldiers, worn out by the war, promised themselves rest.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs bellō fessī sibi quiētem prōmīsērunt.

questions.prompt: The greedy merchant kept all the gold for himself.
questions.answer: Mercātor avārus omne aurum sibi retinuit.

questions.prompt: The philosopher was sufficient unto himself in all matters.
questions.answer: Philosophus sibi ipse in omnibus rēbus sufficiēbat.

questions.prompt: The exile, longing for his homeland, spoke with himself in the night.
questions.answer: Exsul patriae cupidus nocte sēcum loquēbātur.

questions.prompt: Though few, we bravely defended ourselves against many enemies.
questions.answer: Nōs quamquam paucī fortiter contrā multōs hostēs dēfendimus.

questions.prompt: The tyrant surrounded himself with faithful guards.
questions.answer: Tyrannus sē fīdīs custōdibus circumdedit.

questions.prompt: The wise man conquers himself and governs his own desires.
questions.answer: Sapiēns sē vincit et cupiditātēs suās regit.

questions.prompt: The queen adorned herself with jewels before the great feast.
questions.answer: Rēgīna sē gemmīs ante magnum convīvium ōrnāvit.

questions.prompt: The boys were fighting among themselves in the empty forum.
questions.answer: Puerī inter sē in forō vacuō pugnābant.

questions.prompt: You trust yourself too much, my friend.
questions.answer: Nimium tibi cōnfīdis, mī amīce.

questions.prompt: The wounded general dragged himself back into the camp.
questions.answer: Dux vulnerātus sē in castra trāxit.

questions.prompt: I have prepared myself for every danger by long toil.
questions.answer: Mē longō labōre ad omne perīculum parāvī.

questions.prompt: The philosopher, content with himself, despised riches.
questions.answer: Philosophus sē contentus dīvitiās contempsit.

questions.prompt: The enemies betrayed one another out of fear.
questions.answer: Hostēs inter sē metū prōdidērunt.

questions.prompt: Devote yourself to virtue, young man, and flee idleness.
questions.answer: Tē virtūtī trāde, iuvenis, et ōtium fuge.

questions.prompt: To what end will unbridled audacity hurl itself?
questions.answer: Quem ad fīnem sēsē effrēnāta iactābit audācia?

questions.prompt: When they came to Syracuse, Scipio made ready deeds, not words, to clear himself.
questions.answer: Venientibus iīs Syrācūsās Scīpiō rēs, nōn verba ad pūrgandum sēsē parāvit.

questions.prompt: At the same time as the Aedui, the Ambarri, kinsmen and blood-relations of the Aedui, inform Caesar that, their fields having been laid waste, they cannot easily keep the enemy's force away from their towns.
questions.answer: Eōdem tempore quō Haeduī Ambarrī, necessāriī et cōnsanguineī Haeduōrum, Caesarem certiōrem faciunt sēsē dēpopulātīs agrīs nōn facile ab oppidīs vim hostium prohibēre.

questions.prompt: They hope they can get possession of the whole of Gaul.
questions.answer: Tōtīus Galliae sēsē potīrī posse spērant.

questions.prompt: The rest betook themselves to flight.
questions.answer: reliquī sēsē fugae mandārunt.

questions.prompt: They cast themselves at Caesar’s feet.
questions.answer: sēsē Caesarī ad pedēs prōiēcērunt.

questions.prompt: A good many retreated to the town from fear.
questions.answer: multī in oppidum propter timōrem sēsē recipiunt.

questions.prompt: Vorenus did not keep inside the palisade either.
questions.answer: nē Vorēnus quidem sēsē vāllō continet.

questions.prompt: How is every thing in Samnium?
questions.answer: ut sēsē in Samniō rēs habent?

questions.prompt: They made the request in behalf of a pitiable wretch, who would be only too glad to be put to the rack himself, so his father’s death might be investigated.
questions.answer: postulābant prō homine miserrimō, quī vel ipse sēsē in cruciātum darī cuperet, dum dē patris morte quaererētur.

questions.prompt: The case stands thus: the Odyssey in Latin is, you may say, a regular work of Daedalus.
questions.answer: sīc enim sēsē rēs habet: nam Odyssīa Latīna est sīc tamquam opus Daedalī.

questions.prompt: They hoped to carry it out.
questions.answer: id sēsē effectūrōs spērābant.
